name: Interface Synthesizer
description:
Interface for synthesizing OpenBindings interfaces from sources read under their exact kinds. A kind decides how the source is read and may incorporate an artifact authority, have a private definition, or exist only in code.

Carried-values rule: sources and bindings are read under the OpenBindings 0.2 line named by this contract. A source may carry only kind, content, description and x- members. A binding may carry only operation, source, content, idempotent, preference, description, deprecated and x- members, each core member with its core type. The implementation MUST refuse a call carrying any other member or a core member of the wrong type before doing its work. Open carrier schemas preserve extensions; their openness does not waive this rule. Binding operation/source members are forwarded verbatim; this interface neither interprets them nor forbids a kind from reading them. Other binding metadata is information, not an instruction. Kinds are best served identifying targets through content.

For a kind answered false, both synthesis operations refuse before work. For a kind answered true, strict synthesis refuses an unhandled admitted case; synthesis with coverage may disclose it as implementation-unsupported. A wholly unreadable source MUST be refused. When only part of its inventory can be established, synthesis with coverage MAY return a sound partial interface with exhaustive: false and limitation evidence; every established admitted unit the implementation cannot represent is disclosed as implementation-unsupported. Strict synthesis MUST refuse such partial work.

SupportedKind.description: A kind supported for the work this interface performs.

kind.description: Exact, opaque kind as carried by a source.

KindSupportVerdict.description: Authoritative support verdict for one exact kind. Future optional fields may annotate the verdict but never qualify or soften supported.

kind.description: The exact kind supplied by the caller.

supported.description: True warrants that this implementation knows how to read sources of this exact kind, and their bindings, for its job and never presents a case it cannot handle as handled: it refuses before work or, where the operation defines disclosure, omits and discloses the case. False means every call on this kind is refused before work.

SynthesizeInterfaceSource.description: A source to synthesize from, recorded unchanged, including extensions, in the emitted interface under name.

name.description: Key for this source in the emitted interface. Supply it when planning to edit the emitted source.

openbindingsVersion.description: Target specification version. If supplied it MUST name the supported 0.2 line; another line is refused. Omission still targets the 0.2 line.

sources.description: Binding sources to synthesize from. Omission and an empty array both request a source-free skeleton. Every input is preserved as an unchanged emitted source; every emitted source corresponds to an input. Distinct supplied names remain distinct keys. Equal values may share a key where names permit; coverage still accounts for each input index. A repeated explicit name attached to unequal source values is refused before work.

SynthesisCoverageEntry.description: Disposition of one source interaction unit, declared dependency, or separately tracked projection observed during synthesis. An interaction unit is an addressable target or independently selectable alternative whose omission would remove an upstream-permitted invocation path; a dependency is a source unit the synthesizer emitted as a consumption point in the interface's `dependencies` map rather than as a binding, so its omission would remove a declared consumption point rather than an invocation path; a projection records schema or semantic fidelity of a represented path. Every dependency the emitted interface declares in its `dependencies` map has exactly one represented or lossy dependency-scope entry, and a represented dependency entry carries no operation, binding, source key, or reason code. A represented or lossy dependency entry MUST name its emitted dependencyKey; correspondence is a bijection with the emitted dependencies map. Unit identities compare exact sourceIndex, scope and sourceRef. Projection identity additionally includes sourceKey, operationKey and bindingKey when present; repeated or conflicting identities are rejected even for non-exhaustive reports.

sourceIndex.description: Zero-based index of the input source containing the interaction unit. It also indexes coverage.sourceKeys, which preserves the input-to-emitted-source mapping after the request is gone.

sourceKey.description: Key of the corresponding emitted source. Required for represented/lossy target, alternative and projection units; absent on dependency units.

sourceRef.description: Stable source-local identifier for the interaction unit; independent of the shape of any emitted binding content.

scope.description: Whether the unit is an addressable target, an independently selectable alternative of a target, a schema/semantic projection whose fidelity is assessed separately, or a dependency the interface declares as a consumption point rather than binds. Scope names what the source unit is; status names what became of it, so every scope can carry every status. A dependency unit that was not emitted is scope dependency with the status that removed it, not a target.

operationKey.description: Emitted operation key. Required when status is represented or lossy, except on a dependency unit, which is a consumption point and carries no emitted operation or binding identity.

bindingKey.description: Emitted binding key. Required when status is represented or lossy, except on a dependency unit, which carries no emitted binding identity.

reasonCode.description: Stable namespaced reason code for this kind or implementation. Required unless status is represented.

rule.description: Evidence identifying the kind-owned rule governing this disposition, including enough revision information to locate its defining document or code. Required for excluded. An implementation's restriction of a kind defined elsewhere is implementation-unsupported, not excluded.

requirements.description: Named runtime prerequisites for a represented unit, such as credentials or a required codec.

dependencyKey.description: Key of the emitted dependency. Required for represented/lossy dependency entries; forbidden on other entries. Each emitted dependency has exactly one such entry.
Key of the emitted dependency. Required for represented/lossy dependency entries; forbidden on other entries. Each emitted dependency has exactly one such entry.
Key of the emitted dependency. Required for represented/lossy dependency entries; forbidden on other entries. Each emitted dependency has exactly one such entry.

SynthesisCoverage.description: Durable accounting of the source interaction units observed by one synthesis call.

sourceKeys.description: One emitted source key per supplied input, in original request order. Length MUST equal the input sources length (zero when omitted). Each key MUST resolve to the unchanged corresponding input source; a supplied name MUST be used. Repeated keys are allowed for equal inputs where names permit. An unnamed input may map to any equal preserved emitted source; its binding paths may use another equal emitted source. Every entry sourceIndex indexes this array, including non-emitted and dependency entries.

exhaustive.description: True only when every interaction unit in every accepted input source, under the kind's defined inventory, has exactly one disposition. False when the implementation cannot establish that claim.

fullyRepresented.description: Derived as exhaustive AND every entry status is represented or invalid. Excluded, lossy and implementation-unsupported entries in any scope make it false. Invalid units are not upstream-valid units.

CoverageLimitation.description: Machine-readable evidence explaining why the synthesis inventory is not exhaustive.

message.description: Human-readable explanation of what may be missing and why.

details.description: Optional implementation- or kind-specific structured evidence.

SynthesizeInterfaceResult.description: A creation-time-sound OBI and durable coverage evidence derived from the same synthesis observation.

Source.description: A source as an OpenBindings 0.2 document carries it: an exact kind and optional content read under that kind. Absent content and present JSON null are distinct. Only core source fields and x- extensions may appear; the carried-values rule requires refusal of other members before work.

kind.description: The source's kind, compared by exact equality.

content.description: Content read under the source's kind: any JSON value, absent when the source has none.

Binding.description: A binding as an OpenBindings 0.2 document carries it, or would carry it, by value. It is interpreted under the accompanying source's kind. Absent content and present JSON null are distinct. Only core binding fields and x- extensions may appear; the carried-values rule requires refusal of other members before work.

operation.description: The author's operation key, forwarded verbatim without interpretation by this interface.

source.description: The author's source key, forwarded verbatim without interpretation by this interface.

content.description: Content read under the source's kind: any JSON value, absent when the binding has none.

idempotent.description: The binding author's idempotency claim, carried as information.

preference.description: The author's preference signal, carried as information.

deprecated.description: The author's deprecation signal, carried as information.

openbindings.interface-synthesizer.listS.description: Return an advisory list of kinds supported for this interface's job, for display, documentation and pickers. Every listed kind MUST receive supported: true from this interface's checkKindSupport. Absence carries no information and MUST NOT be treated as a negative support decision. This operation is idempotent: repeating it with the same input in context that does not change its intended effects produces no additional intended operation-level effects after the first application. This does not promise identical results or authorize retries.

openbindings.interface-synthesizer.check.description: Authoritatively determine support for exact kinds for this interface's job. This is the only operation on which a consumer may base a support decision. Return one verdict per unique input kind in first-occurrence order. True warrants that the implementation knows how to read the kind for this job, whether its meaning is written, private or defined only in code. True does not promise every case is within reach; an unhandled case is never presented as handled. False means every call on the kind is refused before work. For a kind answered false, both synthesis operations refuse before work. For a kind answered true, strict synthesis refuses an unhandled admitted case; synthesis with coverage may disclose it as implementation-unsupported. A wholly unreadable source MUST be refused. When only part of its inventory can be established, synthesis with coverage MAY return a sound partial interface with exhaustive: false and limitation evidence; every established admitted unit the implementation cannot represent is disclosed as implementation-unsupported. Strict synthesis MUST refuse such partial work. The result is deterministic for a given implementation version and configuration. Kinds compare by exact equality: no normalization, case folding, prefix matching, inferred version order or dereferencing. An internal pattern may compress the supported set but MUST NOT extend it. Future optional verdict fields may annotate a verdict but never qualify supported. This operation is idempotent: repeating it with the same input in context that does not change its intended effects produces no additional intended operation-level effects after the first application. This does not promise identical results or authorize retries. The check MUST have no side effects; it neither acquires nor modifies source artifacts or performs the interface job.

openbindings.interface-synthesizer.synth.description: Synthesize a creation-time-sound OpenBindings interface, optionally from binding source artifacts. Every emitted binding resolves to a supported target and admits a faithful invocation path. For every accepted source input, represent every callable target admitted by its source's kind; an implementation may refuse an unsupported artifact as a whole but MUST refuse instead of silently returning a partial interface when one admitted target cannot be represented faithfully. This operation is idempotent: repeating it with the same input in context that does not change its intended effects produces no additional intended operation-level effects after the first application. This does not promise identical results or authorize retries. Every emitted source is exactly the corresponding supplied source, including extensions and content presence. When name is supplied, use it as the source key. Refuse a supplied openbindingsVersion outside the 0.2 line. The carried-values rule applies. After a caller substitutes source content, the resulting document and the validity of affected bindings are the caller's claim. If the complete admitted inventory cannot be established, strict synthesis MUST refuse instead of returning a partial interface. Strict success requires exhaustive coverage and no implementation-unsupported disposition in any scope, including dependencies, alternatives and projections. Sound lossy representation and invalid or kind-excluded units do not independently prohibit strict success. Strict eligibility is distinct from fullyRepresented. Every emitted operation MUST be referenced by at least one emitted binding or dependency. Dependency-only operations are permitted. This structural requirement is necessary but does not prove kind-specific soundness; it does not require a binding-to-coverage bijection.

Synthesize a creation-time-sound OpenBindings interface and return durable dispositions plus an explicit exhaustiveness claim for the source interaction units considered by the same call. The result distinguishes kind-defined exclusions, invalid source units, lossy projections, and implementation gaps. Coverage is evidence that consumers may verify independently, not proof. This operation is idempotent: repeating it with the same input in context that does not change its intended effects produces no additional intended operation-level effects after the first application. This does not promise identical results or authorize retries. Every emitted source is exactly the corresponding supplied source, including extensions and content presence. When name is supplied, use it as the source key. Refuse a supplied openbindingsVersion outside the 0.2 line. The carried-values rule applies. After a caller substitutes source content, the resulting document and the validity of affected bindings are the caller's claim. A wholly unreadable source MUST be refused. When only part of its inventory can be established, synthesis with coverage MAY return a sound partial interface with exhaustive: false and limitation evidence; every established admitted unit the implementation cannot represent is disclosed as implementation-unsupported. Strict synthesis MUST refuse such partial work. Every emitted operation MUST be referenced by at least one emitted binding or dependency. Dependency-only operations are permitted. This structural requirement is necessary but does not prove kind-specific soundness; it does not require a binding-to-coverage bijection.
